agree.reason: The arithmetic, the June checkpoint, the open admission of a $32,000 first-year shortfall and the offer to the ad sales lead will persuade most of the board, but the two ad-background members will still ask why ads can't run alongside membership, and the memo never answers that.

honest.reason: The firm 'will replace within a year' is offered as a commitment and the risks are stated, but 'so the model works at our scale' rests on one anecdote, 'already shown it can grow faster' rests on a six-week pilot of the keenest readers, and the job offer and 'knows our readers better than anyone' are not in the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives the 20% annual decline, the 150-a-month pilot pace, the 875 target, the 55-a-month pace needed, the 540 midpoint and the roughly $52,000 2027 membership income correctly, but it calls the next year of decline (about $67,000) '2027' when 2026 sits in between.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is shown as a falling trend with a projected figure and the year-one cash gap is set against it, though the projection skips a year and the hybrid option of keeping ads alongside membership is never considered.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint gives a number (540), a date (30 June 2027) and a consequence (a revised plan within 30 days), all of which the board can check, though the consequence is fairly soft.

objections.reason: It deals well with the ad sales lead, churn and the cash dip, but leaves out the objection the ad-background members are most likely to raise, which is why ads must stop entirely rather than run in parallel.

fit.reason: It is a clean board memo with the decision up front, and it is about one page, though slightly dense for that limit.
